The input coordinates are processed byte-by-byte from most significant to least significant.
Extract the top 8 bits of each coordinate: `(z >> 16) & 0xFF`, `(y >> 16) & 0xFF`, `(x >> 16) & 0xFF`.
Look up these values in `morton256_z`, `morton256_y`, and `morton256_x` respectively.
Combine the results with bitwise OR to form the most significant part of the answer.
Extract the middle 8 bits of each coordinate: `(z >> 8) & 0xFF`, `(y >> 8) & 0xFF`, `(x >> 8) & 0xFF`.
Look up these values in the tables and combine with bitwise OR.
Extract the bottom 8 bits of each coordinate: `(z & 0xFF)`, `(y & 0xFF)`, `(x & 0xFF)`.
If the chunk size is limited to $256^3$, the coordinates fit within 8 bits per axis.
